```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
```

```{r config}
index_species <- "{{STOCK_KEY}}"
source(here::here("R", "0_setup.R"))
source(here::here("R", "compile_functions.R"))
source(here::here("R", "plot_helpers.R"))

stock <- cfg$STOCK_KEY
sp <- tolower(cfg$SPECIES_NAME)
Sp <- cfg$SPECIES_NAME
area_label <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste("ICES subareas", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = " and "))
} else cfg$REGION
area_short <- if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) {
  paste0("ICES ", paste(unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), collapse = "–"))
} else cfg$REGION
inside_label <- paste("Inside", area_short)
compiled_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compiled-data.rds")
metadata_path <- file.path(out_dir, "compile-metadata.rds")
# Last complete year: LAST_YEAR in config.yaml, or the year before the current year,
# because the current year's surveys are not yet complete. Numeric literal for DuckDB.
last_year <- as.integer(cfg$LAST_YEAR %||% (as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - 1L))
```

# Purpose

This document selects the IMR bottom-trawl survey data used for the `r sp` (*`r cfg$SPECIES_LATIN`*) survey indices in `r area_label` (stock `r cfg$STOCK_CODE`). `r cfg$PURPOSE`

The document answers which surveys, hauls and catch records enter the indices, and which are excluded and why. Its output is the compiled station dataset in `data/output/`, which is described further in the companion data report ([`r stock`-3-data](`r stock`-3-data.html)) and is the input to the spatiotemporal sdmTMB models [@Vihtakari2026]. Species, survey and model settings are read at run time from `config.yaml`.

```{r compile, eval=params$recompile}
con <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(bes_db_path(), read_only = TRUE))
db_meta <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM metadata")

res <- compile_species_stations(con, cfg, last_year)
dt <- add_response_and_covariates(res$stations, cfg) |>
  clean_tow_speed(cfg$TOW_SPEED_LIMITS %||% c(1.5, 6))
# Hauls positioned in deep water while the recorded depth is shallow have a wrong position.
position_errors <- flag_position_errors(dt, cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500,
                                        cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3)
dt <- dplyr::filter(dt, !haul_id %in% position_errors$haul_id)

# Prediction region: the buffered concave hull of the hauls with the species, cut to the stock
# area. Hauls outside it are zero hauls far from the species' range; they are removed here so
# that the data report, the model fits and every later figure and table use the same hauls.
stock_area <- read_stock_area(cfg, cap = FALSE)
region <- build_stock_region(dt, stock_area, cfg$CRS, buffer_km = cfg$REGION_BUFFER_KM %||% 25,
                             ratio = cfg$REGION_CONCAVITY %||% 0.1, label = cfg$SPECIES_NAME)
region_file <- here::here(cfg$PREDICTION_REGION_FILE %||%
                            file.path(cfg$SOURCE_DIR %||% "data/source",
                                      paste0(stock, "-prediction-region.gpkg")))
dir.create(dirname(region_file), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
sf::st_write(region, region_file, layer = cfg$REGION_LAYER, append = FALSE, quiet = TRUE)
in_region <- dt |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitudestart", "latitudestart"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  sf::st_transform(cfg$CRS) |>
  sf::st_intersects(region) |>
  lengths() > 0
region_removed <- dplyr::select(dt[!in_region, ], haul_id, year, cruiseseries, biomass,
                                 longitudestart, latitudestart)
dt <- dt[in_region, ]

lengths <- collect_lengths(con, cfg, dt)
length_limits <- unlist(cfg$LENGTH_LIMITS %||% c(5, 200)) # plausible lengths (cm)
length_outliers <- dplyr::filter(lengths, length_cm < length_limits[1] |
                                   length_cm > length_limits[2])
lengths <- dplyr::filter(lengths, length_cm >= length_limits[1],
                         length_cm <= length_limits[2])
lw <- fit_length_weight(lengths, cfg$LW_OUTLIER_SD %||% 4)
dt <- add_fishable_biomass(dt, lengths, lw, cfg$OVER_CM)

positive_observations <- collect_positive_observations(con, cfg, last_year)
distance_check <- distance_diagnostics(con, cfg, last_year)
quality_codes <- quality_code_table(con)
other_data <- other_data_summary(con, cfg)
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)

dir.create(here::here("ai", "review"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
readr::write_csv(position_errors,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-position-errors.csv")))
readr::write_csv(res$diagnostics$inconsistent,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-inconsistent-hauls.csv")))
readr::write_csv(res$diagnostics$incomplete,
                 here::here("ai", "review", paste0(stock, "-incomplete-catches.csv")))

compile_metadata <- list(
  data_downloaded_at_label = format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M %Z"),
  db_updated = format(as.POSIXct(db_meta$timeend[1]), "%Y-%m-%d"),
  diagnostics = res$diagnostics[c("n_candidate_rows", "n_valid_hauls",
                                  "n_qualifying_missions", "russian")],
  n_inconsistent = nrow(res$diagnostics$inconsistent),
  n_incomplete = nrow(res$diagnostics$incomplete),
  incomplete_by_series = res$diagnostics$incomplete,
  n_multi_sample = nrow(res$diagnostics$multi_sample),
  lw = lw[c("a", "b", "n")],
  lw_plot = lw$plot,
  lw_outlier_sd = cfg$LW_OUTLIER_SD %||% 4,
  n_lw_outliers = nrow(lw$outliers),
  position_errors = dplyr::select(position_errors, haul_id, year, cruiseseries, platformname,
                                  longitudestart, latitudestart, depth_recorded, depth_gebco,
                                  biomass, count),
  n_speed_flag = sum(dt$speed_flag),
  tow_speed_limits = unlist(cfg$TOW_SPEED_LIMITS %||% c(1.5, 6)),
  length_limits = length_limits,
  n_length_outliers = nrow(length_outliers),
  region_removed = region_removed,
  region_km2 = as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_union(region))) / 1e6,
  positive_observations = positive_observations,
  distance_check = distance_check,
  quality_codes = quality_codes,
  other_data = other_data
)
saveRDS(dt, compiled_path)
saveRDS(lengths, file.path(out_dir, "length-data.rds"))
saveRDS(compile_metadata, metadata_path)
```

```{r load}
dt <- readRDS(compiled_path)
compile_metadata <- readRDS(metadata_path)
dt$cruiseseries <- order_cruise_series(dt$cruiseseries, dt$year)
cs_cols <- cruise_series_colours(levels(dt$cruiseseries))
n_fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = " ")
pct <- function(x, acc = 1) scales::percent(x, accuracy = acc)
included_surveys <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$missionid)
latest <- dplyr::slice_max(dt, start_time, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
region <- sf::read_sf(here::here(cfg$PREDICTION_REGION_FILE %||%
                                   file.path(cfg$SOURCE_DIR %||% "data/source",
                                             paste0(stock, "-prediction-region.gpkg"))))
n_region_removed <- nrow(compile_metadata$region_removed)
n_region_pos <- sum(compile_metadata$region_removed$biomass > 0)
```

# Data

The station and catch data were read from a local copy of the IMR Biotic database compiled with [BioticExplorerServer](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/BioticExplorerServer) [@BioticExplorerServer], last updated on `r compile_metadata$db_updated`, and extracted on `r compile_metadata$data_downloaded_at_label`.

## Stock area

The stock is defined by `r area_label`. The overview map shows all quality-filtered research bottom-trawl hauls with `r sp` in the Northeast Atlantic, coloured by whether the haul lies inside the stock area, together with the prediction region (@sec-prediction-region) inside it (@fig-stock-area). Hauls outside the stock area belong to neighbouring stocks and are not used. Of the `r n_fmt(nrow(compile_metadata$positive_observations))` positive hauls on the map, `r n_fmt(sum(compile_metadata$positive_observations$inside))` lie inside `r area_label`.

```{r stock-area-map}
stock_area <- read_stock_area(cfg)
obs <- compile_metadata$positive_observations |>
  dplyr::mutate(Location = factor(dplyr::if_else(inside, inside_label, "Outside"),
                                  levels = c("Outside", inside_label))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Location)
lim <- unlist(cfg$MAP_LIMITS)

base_area <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(limits = lim, bathymetry = TRUE, bathy.style = "rcb",
                                  bathy.alpha = 0.35, land.col = "grey85",
                                  land.border.col = "grey60", legends = FALSE,
                                  base_size = 9, rotate = TRUE)
area_map_height <- map_fig_height(base_area, extra = 0.7) # before geom_sf() resets limits
p_area <- base_area +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = sf::st_transform(region, 4326), fill = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.2,
                   colour = NA) +
  ggplot2::geom_sf(data = stock_area, fill = NA, colour = "#0072B2", linewidth = 0.6) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(
    data = obs, ggplot2::aes(longitudestart, latitudestart, fill = Location),
    shape = 21, size = 1, stroke = 0.15, colour = "black", crs = 4326
  ) +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = stats::setNames(c("#56B4E9", "#E69F00"),
                                                     c("Outside", inside_label)),
                             name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::guides(fill = ggplot2::guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r, fig.height = area_map_height}
#| label: fig-stock-area
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0(area_label, " (blue outline), the prediction region (blue shading) and quality-filtered research bottom-trawl hauls with ", sp, " in the Northeast Atlantic, ", cfg$FIRST_YEAR, "–", max(dt$year), ". Orange: inside the stock area; light blue: outside. Hauls without ", sp, " are not shown.")'
ggOceanMaps::reorder_layers(p_area)
```

## Haul filter {#sec-haul-filter}

A haul was retained when it met all criteria in @tbl-filter-criteria. The rules follow index-wise `data-filtering.md`; the meaning of each retained quality code is taken from the reference tables of the Biotic database (see also the quality-code documentation of [BAIT](https://github.com/DeepWaterIMR/BAIT)).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-filter-criteria
tibble::tribble(
  ~Field, ~`Retained values`, ~Meaning,
  "gearcategory", "Bottom trawls", "Bottom-trawl gear only",
  "missiontypename", "Forskningsfartøy, Leiefartøy", "Research vessels and chartered vessels; reference fleet, commercial sampling and coast guard excluded",
  "startyear", paste0(cfg$FIRST_YEAR, "–", last_year), "Years included: the first year of regular coverage of the stock area (FIRST_YEAR), and the current year is excluded until its surveys are complete (LAST_YEAR)",
  "Stock area", if (length(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS)) paste0("icesarea ", paste0("27.", unlist(cfg$STOCK_SUBAREAS), ".*", collapse = ", ")) else "inside REGION_FILE polygon", area_label,
  "gearcondition", "1, 2", "1: gear OK; 2: minor damage with no material effect on catch",
  "samplequality", "1 (CoastalS: 1, 2)", "1: preselected position, trawl sensors normal; 2: deployed on an acoustic registration or other fish information, sensors normal",
  "stationtype", "missing, 1, 3, 9, 13", "Missing: ordinary unflagged station; 1: part of a 24-hour station; 3: gear trial that is also a regular fish station; 9: regular fish station; 13: additional preselected station",
  "distance", "0.3–5 nmi", "Towed distance usable for swept area",
  "gear", "not 3100, 3101, 3130", "Unspecified bottom-trawl codes removed",
  "nation", if (isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN)) "all" else "not 140, 90", if (isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN)) "Russian research vessels included (INCLUDE_RUSSIAN)" else "Russian research vessels excluded (INCLUDE_RUSSIAN); their data are confidential",
  "Prediction region", "inside", "Buffered concave hull of the hauls with the species, cut to the stock-area polygons; hauls positioned outside the polygons are removed even when their area code is in the stock (@sec-prediction-region)"
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Haul filter criteria. Hauls meeting all criteria were retained.")
```

The filter was applied in the database before the records were collected; the sample-quality rule, which depends on the cruise series, and the nation rule were applied immediately after collection (@lst-filter-expression). The prediction-region rule was applied last, after the surveys had been selected (@sec-prediction-region).

```{r}
#| lst-label: lst-filter-expression
#| lst-cap: "Haul filter applied to the Biotic `stnall` table (from `standard_haul_filter()`, `apply_samplequality()`, `in_stock_area()` and `compile_species_stations()` in `R/compile_functions.R`)."
#| code-fold: false
#| eval: false
stnall |>
  dplyr::filter(
    gearcategory == "Bottom trawls",
    missiontypename %in% c("Forskningsfartøy", "Leiefartøy"),
    startyear >= cfg$FIRST_YEAR,
    startyear <= last_year,
    !is.na(distance), !is.na(latitudestart), !is.na(longitudestart),
    latitudestart > 0,
    gearcondition %in% c("1", "2"),
    is.na(stationtype) | stationtype %in% c("1", "3", "9", "13"),
    distance >= 0.3, distance <= 5,
    is.na(gear) | !gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130")
  ) |>
  area_filter_lazy(cfg) |>   # ICES-area code (STOCK_SUBAREAS) or polygon bounding box
  dplyr::collect() |>
  dplyr::filter(in_stock_area(dplyr::pick(dplyr::everything()), cfg)) |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(cruiseseriescode) & cruiseseriescode == "23",
      samplequality %in% c("1", "2"),
      samplequality %in% "1"
    ),
    isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN) | !nation %in% c("140", "90")  # Russian research vessels
  )
```

The coastal survey (CoastalS, cruise-series code 23) accepts sample-quality codes 1 and 2, whereas other cruise series require code 1. In its early years the coastal survey targeted saithe acoustically. We assume that `r sp` was nevertheless sampled at random with respect to those registrations, so code 2 hauls are kept for CoastalS.

Missing station types are retained explicitly, because most ordinary stations carry no station type and a database `IN` test would otherwise drop them. `r if (isTRUE(cfg$INCLUDE_RUSSIAN)) paste0("Russian data are included (INCLUDE_RUSSIAN in config.yaml); ", n_fmt(sum(dt$nation %in% c("140", "90"))), " retained hauls are Russian.") else paste0("Hauls from Russian research vessels (nation codes 140 and 90) are excluded (INCLUDE_RUSSIAN in config.yaml), because their data are confidential and add little information on ", sp, ": ", {rus <- compile_metadata$diagnostics$russian; if (is.null(rus)) "they are summarised when the data are next compiled." else if (rus$missions == 0) paste0("no Russian cruise in the area caught ", sp, ".") else paste0("the ", rus$missions, " Russian cruises in the area that caught ", sp, " did so in ", rus$positive, " of their ", n_fmt(rus$hauls), " hauls.")})`

The filter gave `r n_fmt(compile_metadata$diagnostics$n_valid_hauls)` valid hauls in `r area_label`, before the survey selection and the prediction-region rule. Hauls where the length sample exceeded the catch (`r compile_metadata$n_inconsistent %||% compile_metadata$n_duplicates` hauls) and hauls where `r sp` was recorded without a catch weight (`r compile_metadata$n_incomplete` hauls) were removed; their identifiers are listed in `ai/review/`. In `r compile_metadata$n_multi_sample` hauls, `r sp` was recorded in more than one catch sample; these samples were treated as additive and summed.

### Prediction region {#sec-prediction-region}

The models predict density only in and near the area where `r sp` has been caught, so the hauls are restricted to a prediction region before any further step. The region is the concave hull of all retained hauls with `r sp`, buffered by `r cfg$REGION_BUFFER_KM` km and cut to the `r area_label` polygons (@fig-stock-area). The region never extends outside these polygons: otherwise the buffer would carry it into the neighbouring stock areas, where the haul filter has removed the data, and the models would predict density where they have no observations. The buffer is wide enough to merge isolated hauls into the region instead of leaving circles around them, and to take in the zero hauls next to the occupied area, such as those deeper on the continental slope, which inform the depth effect and the low densities at the edge of the distribution. Areas with only zero observations are left out. The region covers `r n_fmt(round(compile_metadata$region_km2, -2))` km². The rule removed `r n_fmt(n_region_removed)` hauls of the included surveys (`r round(100 * n_region_removed / (n_region_removed + nrow(dt)))` %). `r if (n_region_pos == 0) paste0('All were zero hauls far from where ', sp, ' occurs.') else paste0('Most were zero hauls far from where ', sp, ' occurs; ', n_region_pos, ' caught ', sp, ' (', round(100 * sum(compile_metadata$region_removed$biomass) / (sum(compile_metadata$region_removed$biomass) + sum(dt$biomass)), 1), ' % of the catch) but lie outside the polygons although their ICES area code is in ', area_short, '.')` The polygons are those that BioticExplorerServer used to assign the ICES area code (`icesarea`) to each station [@BioticExplorerServer], so the area-code filter and the region agree. The ICES areas are the polygons that the Biotic database used to assign each haul its ICES area (`r cfg$ICES_AREAS_FILE %||% "BioticExplorerServer::icesAreas"`), with the boundary between divisions 4.a and 2.a along 62° N, as the areas are defined in Annex III of Regulation (EC) No 218/2009 [@EC2009Reg218]. The region is saved as `r cfg$PREDICTION_REGION_FILE` and used by the data report, the model fits and the prediction grid.

### Tow distance and unspecified gear

The tow-distance limits (0.3–5 nmi) are the generic index-wise rule developed for other species. To check them for `r sp`, @fig-tow-distance shows the distribution of tow distance for all hauls that passed the other haul criteria and for hauls with `r sp`. `r dc <- compile_metadata$distance_check; pos <- dplyr::filter(dc, catch_kg > 0); paste0("Of the ", n_fmt(nrow(pos)), " hauls with ", sp, ", ", sum(pos$distance < 0.3, na.rm = TRUE), " were shorter than 0.3 nmi, ", sum(pos$distance > 5, na.rm = TRUE), " longer than 5 nmi and ", sum(is.na(pos$distance)), " lacked a distance, so the limits keep ", round(100 * mean(pos$distance >= 0.3 & pos$distance <= 5, na.rm = TRUE), 1), " % of them")`. In hauls with `r sp`, the median catch per nautical mile decreased with tow distance (@tbl-tow-distance). This is partly a selection effect, because a short tow catches the species mainly where it is dense, so it does not show that catches fail to scale with tow length. The shortest tows are, however, the most sensitive to errors in the recorded distance. We therefore kept the generic limits for `r sp`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-tow-distance
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Tow distance of all hauls passing the other haul criteria and of hauls with ", sp, " (logarithmic scale). Dashed lines: the 0.3 and 5 nmi limits.")'
dc <- compile_metadata$distance_check |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(distance), distance > 0)
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(dc, group = "All hauls"),
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::filter(dc, catch_kg > 0), group = paste("Hauls with", sp))
) |>
  ggplot(aes(distance)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "#0072B2", colour = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(0.3, 5), linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  facet_wrap(~group, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Tow distance (nmi)", y = "Hauls")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-tow-distance
dc |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Distance (nmi)` = cut(distance, c(0, 0.3, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, Inf))) |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Distance (nmi)`) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(catch_kg > 0),
                   `Median catch (kg)` = round(stats::median(catch_kg[catch_kg > 0]), 1),
                   `Median catch per nmi (kg)` = round(stats::median(catch_kg[catch_kg > 0] /
                                                                    distance[catch_kg > 0]), 1),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Hauls and ", sp, " catches by tow distance, before the distance filter. Medians are for hauls with ", sp, "."))
```

The unspecified bottom-trawl codes (3100, 3101, 3130) occurred in `r sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130"))` hauls, of which `r sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130") & compile_metadata$distance_check$catch_kg > 0)` caught `r sp` (`r round(100 * sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$gear %in% c("3100", "3101", "3130") & compile_metadata$distance_check$catch_kg > 0) / sum(compile_metadata$distance_check$catch_kg > 0), 1)` % of the hauls with `r sp`).

## Surveys and cruise series

A survey means one cruise. A survey was included when at least one positive `r sp` catch passed the haul filter inside `r area_label` (the encountered-on-a-cruise rule). All valid hauls of an included survey were retained, so hauls without `r sp` in those surveys are true zeros: the species would have been recorded had it been caught. Other surveys in the same cruise series were not included unless they also caught `r sp`. Included surveys were afterwards grouped by cruise series; surveys without a cruise-series code, and those of cruise series with few surveys in the stock area, were grouped as `Other` only after they qualified.

The rule selected `r included_surveys` surveys and `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` hauls (@tbl-survey-selection). `r cs_top <- dt |> dplyr::count(cruiseseries, wt = biomass > 0, sort = TRUE); paste0(cs_top$cruiseseries[1], " and ", cs_top$cruiseseries[2])` contributed most positive hauls (`r round(100 * sum(cs_top$n[1:2]) / sum(cs_top$n))` %).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-survey-selection
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Code = {codes <- unique(stats::na.omit(dplyr::na_if(cruiseseriescode, "NA")))
            paste(codes[order(as.numeric(sub(",.*", "", codes)))], collapse = ", ")},
    Surveys = dplyr::n_distinct(missionid),
    `First year` = min(year), `Last year` = max(year),
    Months = format_months(month),
    Hauls = dplyr::n(),
    `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
    `Catch (kg)` = round(sum(biomass)),
    `Zero fraction (%)` = round(100 * mean(biomass == 0), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Cruise series of the included surveys with ", sp,
                                " in ", area_label, ". Zero fraction is the percentage of retained hauls without ", sp, "."))
```

Surveys grouped as `Other` either have no cruise-series code or belong to cruise series with few surveys in the stock area. They are listed one by one in @tbl-other-surveys, with the short name of the cruise series where a code exists, so that each survey can be judged separately. `r oth <- dt |> dplyr::summarise(hauls = mean(cruiseseries == "Other"), pos = sum(cruiseseries == "Other" & biomass > 0) / max(1, sum(biomass > 0)), .by = "year") |> dplyr::filter(year < 2004); if (nrow(oth)) paste0("The Other surveys are concentrated in the early years: before 2004 they hold up to ", pct(max(oth$hauls)), " of the hauls and up to ", pct(max(oth$pos)), " of the hauls with ", sp, " of a year, so the early part of the index depends on them more than the later part. The report tests this with refits without the Other surveys and with the major series only.") else ""`

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other-surveys
dt |>
  dplyr::filter(cruiseseries == "Other") |>
  dplyr::group_by(Year = year, Vessel = platformname, Cruise = cruise,
                  Series = survey_label(cruiseseriescode, series_short, cruise, cfg)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Months = format_months(month),
                   Gear = paste(sort(unique(geartype)), collapse = ", "),
                   Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Included surveys grouped as Other. Series gives the short name and code of the cruise series, or the survey name from SURVEY_NAMES in config.yaml for surveys without a code; – means neither is known.")
```

# Analysis

## Survey catch and effort

Catch is the total recorded `r sp` biomass per haul, and occurrence is the number of positive hauls. The cruise series differ in both, and they do not rank identically by catch and by positive hauls (@fig-survey-catch-overview). Split by year, the same quantities show when each series entered the time series and how uneven the annual coverage is (@fig-survey-catch-year).

```{r}
#| label: fig-survey-catch-overview
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Total ", sp, " catch (t) and number of positive hauls by cruise series. The panels use independent y-axis scales.")'
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(`Total catch (t)` = sum(biomass) / 1000,
                   `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-cruiseseries) |>
  ggplot(aes(cruiseseries, value, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols, guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-survey-catch-year
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Annual number of positive ", sp, " hauls (A) and total catch (B) by cruise series.")'
annual <- dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(year, cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::summarise(positive = sum(biomass > 0), catch_t = sum(biomass) / 1000,
                   .groups = "drop")
p1 <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, positive, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Positive hauls", fill = "Cruise series") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
p2 <- ggplot(annual, aes(year, catch_t, fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Catch (t)", fill = "Cruise series") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
cowplot::plot_grid(p1, p2, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", rel_heights = c(4, 5.2))
```

## Survey positions

The cruise series cover overlapping but different parts of the stock area, and positive hauls are a spatially clustered subset of the effort in every series (@fig-survey-positions).

```{r survey-positions-map}
n_series <- dplyr::n_distinct(dt$cruiseseries)
p_pos <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(data = dt, legends = FALSE, base_size = 8, rotate = TRUE,
                              expand.factor = 1, land.col = "grey85",
                              land.border.col = "grey60") +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dplyr::filter(dt, biomass == 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), colour = "grey40", size = 0.15, alpha = 0.5,
    crs = 4326) +
  ggspatial::geom_spatial_point(data = dplyr::filter(dt, biomass > 0),
    aes(longitudestart, latitudestart), colour = "#D55E00", size = 0.5, crs = 4326) +
  facet_wrap(~cruiseseries, ncol = 3) +
  theme(axis.title = element_blank(), axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank())
positions_map_height <- map_fig_height(p_pos, ncol = 3, nrow = ceiling(n_series / 3),
                                       extra = 0.3 * ceiling(n_series / 3), side = 0.3)
```

```{r, fig.height = positions_map_height}
#| label: fig-survey-positions
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Retained hauls by cruise series. Grey: hauls without ", sp, " (true zeros); orange: hauls with ", sp, ".")'
p_pos
```

## Gear

`r widths_txt <- paste0(names(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS), " ", unlist(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS), " m", collapse = ", "); if (!length(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS)) paste0("All catches were converted to density using a common ", cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, " m effective width.") else paste0("Catches were converted to density with an effective width for each trawl: ", cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, " m for the Campelen shrimp trawl and every gear without its own width, and ", widths_txt, " for the cod trawls (the Campelen width scaled by the ratio of the wing spreads; for the Alfredo III trawl the wing spread is 10.1 + 0.142 × door spread [@Nogueira2020SCR015])", if ("trawldoorspread" %in% names(dt) && all(c("Cod", "Shrimp") %in% dt$geartype[!is.na(dt$trawldoorspread)])) { door <- dplyr::summarise(dt, m = stats::median(trawldoorspread, na.rm = TRUE), .by = "geartype"); paste0(" (median recorded door spread ", round(door$m[door$geartype == "Cod"]), " m against ", round(door$m[door$geartype == "Shrimp"]), " m for the shrimp trawls)") } else "", ".", if (length(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS_DOOR)) " The report tests wider cod-trawl widths scaled by the door spread, which would apply if the doors and sweeps herded the fish into the trawl path." else "")` `r if (any(c("geartype", "fgear") %in% unlist(cfg$FINAL_MODEL$TERMS))) "Gear type is a fixed effect in the final models, so systematic gear differences are estimated." else "Gear type was tested as a fixed effect in the model selection and dropped, because the model without it predicted the held-out hauls as well; the final models therefore assume the same catchability for both gear types."` `r gt <- dplyr::count(dt, geartype, sort = TRUE); paste0(gt$geartype[1], " trawls")` account for `r round(100 * gt$n[1] / sum(gt$n))` % of the hauls (@fig-gear-overview). Depth, tow distance and haul duration differ between cruise series and gears (@tbl-gear).

```{r}
#| label: fig-gear-overview
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: !expr 'paste0("Gear used in the included surveys. A: ", sp, " catch per positive haul by gear (number of hauls in brackets), coloured by cruise series, logarithmic scale. B: number of hauls by year and gear type.")'
gear_n <- dplyr::count(dt, gearname, name = "n_hauls")
gd <- dt |>
  dplyr::filter(biomass > 0) |>
  dplyr::left_join(gear_n, by = "gearname") |>
  dplyr::mutate(gear_label = paste0(gearname, " (", n_hauls, ")"))
p_gear <- ggplot(gd, aes(stats::reorder(gear_label, biomass, FUN = median), biomass,
                         fill = cruiseseries)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.5, outlier.alpha = 0.3, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::label_number(drop0trailing = TRUE)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cs_cols) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Catch per positive haul (kg)", fill = "Cruise series") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "right")
p_year <- dt |>
  dplyr::count(year, geartype) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, n, fill = geartype)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gear_colours()) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(1980, 2030, 5), expand = expansion(mult = 0.01)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Hauls", fill = "Gear type")
cowplot::plot_grid(p_gear, p_year, ncol = 1, labels = "AUTO", rel_heights = c(6, 4),
                   align = "v", axis = "lr")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-gear
fmt_range <- function(x, digits = 1) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return("–")
  sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f [%.", digits, "f–%.", digits, "f]"), mean(x), min(x), max(x))
}
dt |>
  dplyr::group_by(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries, `Gear type` = geartype, Gear = gearname) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Hauls = dplyr::n(), `Positive hauls` = sum(biomass > 0),
                   `Depth (m)` = fmt_range(depth, 0),
                   `Distance (nmi)` = fmt_range(distance, 2),
                   `Duration (min)` = fmt_range(duration_min, 0),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Gear and haul characteristics by cruise series. Values are mean [minimum–maximum].")
```

## Survey timing

```{r timing-height}
timing_height <- round(0.2 * dplyr::n_distinct(dt$year) + 1.2, 1)
```

The cruise series occupy characteristic and largely stable parts of the year, so season is partly confounded with cruise series (@fig-survey-timing). `r switch(month_term(cfg), smooth = "Month is included as a smooth term in the models; because of the confounding, it also absorbs catchability differences between cruise series that sample in different months.", factor = "Month is included as a factor in the models; because of the confounding, it also absorbs catchability differences between cruise series that sample in different months.", none = paste0("The ", sp, " models have no month term: ", month_term_reason(dt$month, dt$biomass > 0, sp), "."))` A cruise-series factor is tested in the model selection, and the influence of each series on the index is examined in the report (leave-one-survey-out).

```{r, fig.height = timing_height}
#| label: fig-survey-timing
#| fig-cap: "Timing of the included surveys, newest year at the top. Segments span the first to last retained haul of each survey; cruise series are offset slightly within a year."
plot_survey_timing(dt, cs_cols)
```

Survey identity is therefore confounded with season, area and gear: each cruise series samples its own part of the area in its own season, mostly with one trawl (@tbl-confounding, @fig-survey-positions, @tbl-gear). A difference between the series in the model can thus reflect catchability or a real difference in availability, and the two cannot be separated from these data alone. The model selection tests a cruise-series factor and the trawl model, and the report judges the index on its trend in refits without single series and with the major series only.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-confounding
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'paste0("Hauls (with ", sp, " in brackets) by cruise series and quarter of the year, with the main trawl model and the median position and bottom depth of the hauls.")'
dt |>
  dplyr::mutate(quarter = paste0("Q", (month - 1) %/% 3 + 1)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(n = paste0(dplyr::n(), " (", sum(biomass > 0), ")"), .by = c("cruiseseries", "quarter")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = quarter, values_from = n, values_fill = "", names_sort = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dt |> dplyr::summarise(
    `Main trawl` = names(sort(table(gearname), decreasing = TRUE))[1],
    `Median lat (°N)` = round(stats::median(latitudestart), 1),
    `Median lon (°E)` = round(stats::median(longitudestart), 1),
    `Median depth (m)` = round(stats::median(depth, na.rm = TRUE)), .by = "cruiseseries"), by = "cruiseseries") |>
  dplyr::arrange(cruiseseries) |>
  dplyr::rename(`Cruise series` = cruiseseries) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Gross-error screening

Recorded depths, positions, tow durations and length and weight records were screened for gross errors (@tbl-screening). Hauls positioned deeper than `r cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500` m on GEBCO while their recorded bottom depth is shallower than the GEBCO depth divided by `r cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3`, or missing, cannot have fished where they are positioned; the trawls were bottom trawls, and neither species lives pelagically. These hauls are removed, because their position is wrong (`r nrow(compile_metadata$position_errors)` hauls, `r sum(compile_metadata$position_errors$biomass > 0)` with `r sp`; listed in `ai/review/`). The towed distance is taken as correct, because it defines the swept area: where distance and duration imply a speed outside `r paste(compile_metadata$tow_speed_limits, collapse = '–')` knots, the duration is set to missing and the haul is kept. The length–weight outliers are individual weights that deviate strongly from the log-length–log-weight regression; they are left out of that regression, which predicts the weight of each measured fish for the fishable share, but the fish stay in the length data. Depth mismatches are reported but not removed, because the recorded depth is the better measure on steep slopes; they are examined in the data report.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-screening
tibble::tibble(
  Check = c("Depth missing or non-positive; filled from GEBCO",
            "Recorded depth differs from GEBCO by more than a factor of 2",
            "Haul on land according to GEBCO (depth ≤ 0)",
            paste0("Length records outside ", compile_metadata$length_limits[1], "–",
                   compile_metadata$length_limits[2], " cm (removed)"),
            paste0("Hauls with a wrong position (GEBCO depth > ", cfg$POSITION_ERROR_DEPTH %||% 1500, " m, recorded depth < GEBCO / ", cfg$POSITION_ERROR_RATIO %||% 3, " or missing; removed)"),
            paste0("Tow speed (distance / duration) outside ", paste(compile_metadata$tow_speed_limits, collapse = "–"), " knots (duration set to missing; haul kept)"),
            paste0("Individual weights with |standardised residual| > ", compile_metadata$lw_outlier_sd %||% 4, " in the log-length–log-weight regression (left out of the length–weight regression used to predict weight at length; fish kept in the length data)"),
            "Positive hauls without length measurements"),
  Count = c(sum(dt$depth_source == "GEBCO"),
            sum(dt$depth_ratio > 2 | dt$depth_ratio < 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(dt$depth_gebco <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            compile_metadata$n_length_outliers,
            nrow(compile_metadata$position_errors),
            compile_metadata$n_speed_flag,
            compile_metadata$n_lw_outliers,
            sum(dt$biomass > 0 & dt$n_measured == 0))
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("Gross-error screening of the compiled ", sp, " data."))
```

## Other data in the database

The database also holds `r sp` records from the reference fleet, commercial sampling and coast-guard inspections, mostly from longlines and gillnets (@tbl-other-data). These are not survey hauls with a known swept area and are not used for the trawl indices. The reference-fleet longline lengths were used only to set the fishable-length threshold (`r cfg$OVER_CM` cm).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-other-data
compile_metadata$other_data |>
  dplyr::rename(`Mission type` = missiontypename, `Gear category` = gearcategory,
                Stations = stations, `First year` = first_year, `Last year` = last_year) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("All IMR Biotic stations with ", sp, " in ", area_label, " by mission type and gear category, before filtering."))
```

# Results and recommendations

The compiled station dataset is written to `data/output/`, which is git-ignored.

**Ready for downstream use.** The dataset contains `r n_fmt(nrow(dt))` bottom-trawl hauls from `r included_surveys` surveys in `r min(dt$year)`–`r max(dt$year)`, of which `r n_fmt(sum(dt$biomass > 0))` caught `r sp` (@tbl-data-overview). Its zeros are true zeros: hauls of surveys that recorded `r sp` when it was caught. Gear type, depth, month and cruise series are available for every haul.

**Assumptions.** `r if (length(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS)) paste0("The gear-specific widths assume that each trawl samples the path given by its width in config.yaml (GEAR_WIDTHS)", if (length(cfg$GEAR_WIDTHS_DOOR)) ", without extra herding by the doors and sweeps (tested in the report)" else "", ";") else paste0("The common ", cfg$GEAR_WIDTH, " m effective width assumes that the trawls sample the same width;")` `r if (any(c("geartype", "fgear") %in% unlist(cfg$FINAL_MODEL$TERMS))) "the gear fixed effect absorbs systematic differences." else "with gear type dropped from the final models, the models also assume the same catchability for all gear types."` `r if ("CoastalS" %in% dt$cruiseseries) { sq2 <- dt$cruiseseries == "CoastalS" & dt$samplequality %in% "2"; paste0("Keeping sample-quality code 2 for CoastalS assumes that ", sp, " was sampled at random with respect to the acoustic registrations: ", n_fmt(sum(sq2)), " hauls with code 2 are kept, of which ", n_fmt(sum(sq2 & dt$biomass > 0)), " caught ", sp, " (", round(100 * sum(sq2 & dt$biomass > 0) / sum(dt$biomass > 0)), " % of the hauls with ", sp, ").") } else ""` The current year is excluded until its surveys are complete (`LAST_YEAR` in `config.yaml`).

**Decisions.** Every cruise series that passed the encountered-on-a-cruise rule is kept, including the irregular `Other` surveys, and all gear types are kept; the influence of each series on the index is examined in the report. SPD files are `r if (isTRUE(cfg$USE_SPD)) "used" else "not used"`, and the series starts in `r cfg$FIRST_YEAR`.
